body.x: Mikwang EnTech Co., Ltd. (CEO Donghoon Oh) announced its participation in the Global Media Meetup on September 5, an event co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo to present Korean startups’ products and technologies to global markets. The event also spotlighted CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and CES participants to provide worldwide exposure and business opportunities.

Since its founding in 2006, Mikwang EnTech has focused on LED lighting and smart power control, developing next-generation lighting solutions that combine energy efficiency and smart control technology. Based in Pohang Technopark, the company operates a headquarters, a factory, and an R&D center. It holds numerous certifications, including KS, high-efficiency and eco-friendly labels, CE, G-PASS, Inno-Biz, and Main-Biz, as well as designation as a superior product supplier by the Public Procurement Service.

Its core strengths include graphene composite-based high-thermal-dissipation and high-efficiency LED design, smart IoT wireless controllers (BLE, Wi-Fi, MQTT), real-time diagnostics with modular design for optimal maintenance, and waterproof and explosion-proof technologies for industrial and outdoor environments. These capabilities have been applied to smart city lighting, industrial LEDs, and public infrastructure projects in Korea and abroad.

The company has demonstrated stability and reliability in major industrial projects, including supplying high-bay LEDs and waterproof/explosion-proof lighting to POSCO steel plants, as well as high-efficiency LEDs for nuclear facility equipment at the Kori Nuclear Power Plant. It also carried out Pohang City’s public lighting replacement project, strengthening its position in the smart city sector.

Leveraging these achievements, Mikwang EnTech has expanded into overseas markets, supplying waterproof/explosion-proof LEDs, as well as smart IoT wireless controllers, for EU CE-certified markets, UAE industrial complexes, and public projects in Vietnam. The company now plans to accelerate entry into the U.S. market, highlighting its electronics lifespan prediction technology and graphene-based thermal management as unique strengths for competitiveness in smart city and industrial LED lighting.

Mikwang EnTech’s CES 2026 Innovation Award entry, the smart IoT wireless lighting controller, supports BLE, Wi-Fi, and MQTT communication. It integrates power detection, fault diagnostics, and wireless transmission into a single design.

The device features electronics lifespan prediction, enabling proactive maintenance by forecasting the remaining lifespan based on usage and condition data. Graphene-based thermal management solves LED overheating issues, ensuring both high efficiency and stability. OTA updates allow continuous performance improvements even after installation.

Its fault diagnosis function automatically identifies issues with converters, modules, or power supplies. An emergency diagnostic mode transmits alerts via battery-based wireless communication even during external power outages. The compact, modular design makes the controller easy to install and maintain across various industrial, commercial, and public infrastructure settings. Damaged parts can be replaced individually, reducing costs and environmental impact. Real-time smartphone app monitoring and control also enhance user convenience.

Beyond lighting, Mikwang EnTech’s solution has the potential to expand into intelligent transport systems, public facility energy management, and EV charging infrastructure, reinforcing its role as a smart infrastructure platform. The product delivers up to 40% energy savings, reduces power consumption and waste through extended lifespan, and improves maintenance efficiency, contributing to global sustainability goals.

body.cap: Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo (left), and CEO Donghoon Oh of Mikwang EnTech (right) take a commemorative photo at the Global Media Meetup held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 5 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: CEO Donghoon Oh said, “Challenging for the CES 2026 Innovation Award itself is a meaningful leap for Mikwang EnTech. CES will be an opportunity to showcase our proven technologies from major Korean industrial sites, global supply experience in Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia, and the differentiation of our smart IoT controllers and high-efficiency LED technology.” He added that this will serve as a stepping stone for entry into the North American market, expanded partnerships, and overseas revenue growth.

Starting with CES 2026, Mikwang EnTech plans full-scale global market expansion. It will also participate in international exhibitions, such as Light+Building 2026 in Frankfurt, Middle East Energy in Dubai, and the Vietnam International Lighting Exhibition, to strengthen brand recognition in Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.

On the technology side, the company will continue to advance its lifespan prediction algorithms, scale up commercialization of graphene-based thermal management, and develop solutions integrated with smart city infrastructure.

CEO Oh remarked, “We aim to become a company that contributes to solving global challenges of carbon neutrality and energy efficiency in the lighting and energy market, while also bridging academia and industry to nurture next-generation talent.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
